Class Game

java.lang.Object
Game
public class Game extends Object
Game holds the players and the rules of one Nuggets game.

It keeps up to 26 players in fixed slots and the current spectators, and applies joins, quits, moves, swaps, and gold pickup. It builds each client's display string and the game-over summary. It asks Grid about the board: the map, the gold piles, and what is visible from a point.

Game never sends messages. Server calls Game, then sends the results and strings to clients, so Game can be tested with no network.

A player who quits keeps its slot, so its letter is never reused and it stays in the final summary. Game is not thread-safe; the server uses one thread.

    • addPlayer

      public Player addPlayer(String name, InetSocketAddress address)
      Creates the next player and drops it on a random empty room spot, meaning a room spot with no gold and no active player. The player gets the next unused letter and an empty purse, and starts with what it can see from that spot. The player is stored in the next free slot and remembered by address.
      Parameters:
      name - the player's name, already cleaned by cleanName(String)
      address - the address of the client that sent PLAY
      Returns:
      the new player, or null if the game is full or no room spot is free

      Parameters:

    • move

      public int move(Player player, int dr, int dc, boolean sprint)
      Moves a player one step in a direction, or repeatedly until blocked if sprinting.

      The direction is (dr, dc), row first: (0, 1) is right and (-1, 0) is up, because row 0 is the top. A step is allowed only onto a room spot or passage spot. Moving onto another active player swaps the two places. On every step the player collects any gold there, and its visible and known sets are updated, so gridpoints seen in the middle of a sprint stay on its map. A swapped player's sets are updated too. A sprint also stops when no gold remains.

      Parameters:
      player - the player to move; must be active
      dr - the row change per step: -1, 0, or 1
      dc - the column change per step: -1, 0, or 1
      sprint - true to repeat the step until it is blocked
      Returns:
      the total nuggets collected during this move; 0 if none, or if the first step was blocked

    • displayFor

      public String displayFor(Player player)
      Builds one player's display string, drawn in layers. First the map the player has ever seen, then gold piles currently in view, then other active players currently in view, and last the player's own position as '@'. Gold and players that are out of view are not drawn.

      The string has one line per grid row, each exactly as wide as the grid and ending in a newline, as the DISPLAY message requires.

      Parameters:
      player - the player whose display to build
      Returns:
      the display string for that player
      See Also:
      • rowsToString(char[][])

    • spectatorDisplay

      public String spectatorDisplay()
      Builds the spectator's display string: the whole map, every gold pile, and every active player's letter. There is no '@', because a spectator is not on the map. Uses the same line format as displayFor(Player).
      Returns:
      the full-view display string

    • summary

      public String summary()
      Builds the rows of the game-over table, one per player who ever joined, including players who quit. Each row is the letter, the purse right-aligned in 10 columns, and the name, in letter order. Rows are joined by newlines with no trailing newline. Server adds the "GAME OVER:" heading.
      Returns:
      the summary rows; an empty string if no one ever joined
